acceptance: kill_group, after verifying the group and before its first signal, reads ps -A -o pid=,ppid=,pgid=,lstart= once (lstart parsed as the rest of the line, compared as start_token compares it) and records every transitive descendant (by parent pid) of the group's members that is outside the group, with its start time

After the group is gone, each recorded descendant still alive with the same start time gets SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after the grace; a pid authoritatively absent or whose start time differs is gone and never signalled; a survivor, or a failed, timed-out or unparsable descendant inventory or recheck, raises WorkerError naming the pid or the failure (the group itself is still signalled as today), so terminate does not report terminated

', '; ' or a conjunction (and, but, while) is checked on its own; a comma list is several observations, split into lines; evidence goes in commands_rerun. Repair turn: when review record refuses the filed answer, review delegate runs exactly one repair phase: `_attempts` once more, with the existing capacity-retry budget, given (full prompt plus the repair section, the repair section alone), so a resumed launch and every capacity retry carry the refusal and a non-resumable harness gets one fresh launch with the full prompt plus the repair section. The repair section carries the whole refusal text as review record printed it (every offending line, never truncated) in a fence longer than any backtick run in it, the notes rules section, and 'send the whole corrected JSON object'. A snapshot taken right before the repair launch is compared with one after it by the existing write check, model_check is recomputed from the repair attempt's own log span, and the launch keeps the same read-only restrictions. A parse or schema rerun request, a review failure (a write) and a chore reviewer get no repair turn

Run record: RUN-<model>.json lists both turns' attempts, the repair turn's marked `repair: true`, and keeps the first refusal text as `refusal`; a second refusal leaves the run incomplete, exit 1, with a reason naming both refusals. `review delegate --resume` sends the repair prompt pair instead of RESUME_PROMPT only when the stored record's state is `incomplete`, its commit is the one under review and its `refusal` is a string; otherwise (a complete run, no refusal, a non-string refusal, with no traceback) --resume is unchanged
